paragraphs: Bar Yomei: Bammeh Tomnin 49b, end: ‘One of the rabbis, bar yomei, raised an objection to Rava.’ Rashi explains that on that day he entered the study house, or entered authority. The one who explains this as Rabbi Idi, Rabbi Yaakov’s father—see his entry—erred. How could Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi’s father come before Rava, when Rabbi Yaakov the son was Rabbi Yochanan’s colleague, as Rabbi Yochanan said of him, ‘Like our colleague, the son of Idi,’ in Yevamot; see his entry? Moreover, one was in the Land of Israel, and the other in Babylonia.
